## brobot
These tools reach the app you are running inside. An agent is named by the piece of work it owns: W1.2 means the conversation that owns W1.2, and every tool that takes an agent takes that label as well as its id. create_agent brings an agent into existence, optionally with standing rules; give_work gives an agent a piece of work, and with new: true brings a new agent with none into existence as it gives; when the person asks for something to be done, take_on_work takes it on as a piece of your conversation’s own work, so the person can see it and what you give out for it hangs under it; update_work says where a piece stands and keeps files for it — any piece you hold, your own conversation’s work included, or one you gave — titles your own conversation’s work or a piece you gave, and gives a new brief to or closes only a piece you gave: those two are for a piece one conversation gives another. A refusal is a successful call whose payload names the rule that stopped it, whether that rule is permanent, and whether retrying could ever help — read it rather than retrying a permanent one.
